narrative.overview:
One compact top bar, a deck-list home, plain study content and optional help behind disclosures. Keep the warm Oftly identity while reducing visual stimulation.

Light and Dark are appearances of the same quiet tool. The public research page is a Read surface within that world: larger Bricolage headings, readable Atkinson copy, flat chapters and diagrams with their sources beside them. It does not change the density of studying or deck selection.
keyCharacteristics: Flat warm surfaces and fine separators.
Compact top navigation and centered deck rows.
Stable question/answer layout with small, neutral ratings.
Paired Light and Dark appearances with device-local preference and semantic contrast.
Native daily-time fields or centered touch wheels chosen by input capability.
Flat research chapters, larger Read headings and directly sourced diagrams.

rules.name: The Semantic Pair Rule
rules.body: Pair an action background with `on-action`, body surfaces with `ink`, and a story ground with `story-ink`. Use the active CSS roles rather than inverting an entire page or assuming an action always has light text.

rules.name: The Reading Scale Rule
rules.body: Use the larger Read hierarchy for explanatory pages. Preserve the compact interface and study hierarchy for daily work.

dos: Keep the original wordmark and self-hosted fonts.
Use a compact hierarchy and plain counts.
Preserve accessible targets, keyboard controls and text wrapping.
Do use semantic foreground/background pairs in both appearances and retain a visible leaf focus ring.
Do choose study-time wheels by coarse-pointer capability, preserve exact existing minute values and keep native page scrolling.
Do keep research figures labeled, sources adjacent and reduced-motion alternatives complete.
donts: Do not restore a dark rail, dashboard panels or decorative study marks.
Do not hide essential questions, answers or error messages.
Don't tint imported media or Google artwork with a page-wide dark-mode filter.
Don't present an illustrative curve, scheduling target or simulation as a measured product outcome.
